title: Account ledger with atomic transfers
prompt: Build a CLI reading a JSON array of operations from stdin and applying them in order to an in-memory ledger. Each operation is {id,type,...}: deposit {account,amount}, withdraw {account,amount} or transfer {from,to,amount}. id is a nonempty string, accounts match [a-z0-9-]{1,20}, amount is a string of digits with an optional fractional part of 1 or 2 digits, greater than zero and at most 1000000000.00. Accounts are created with balance 0 by their first deposit only. Evaluate each operation in this order and stop at the first reason: shape not valid (including unknown fields) gives status rejected reason invalid; an id that belongs to an earlier applied operation gives status duplicate when the operation is identical to it (same fields) and otherwise rejected reason id_conflict; a transfer with from equal to to gives rejected same_account; an unknown account gives rejected unknown_account (for a transfer both accounts must exist); a withdraw or transfer that would take a balance below zero gives rejected insufficient_funds. Otherwise the operation is applied with status applied. A rejected or duplicate operation changes nothing and its id is not remembered (except that duplicate refers to an earlier applied one). Transfers are atomic. Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {balances,history}. balances maps every account to its balance as a string with exactly 2 decimals; history has one entry per operation in input order as {id,status} plus reason for rejections (id is null when the operation has no string id). A non-array root or invalid JSON: exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
